1	---
2	
3	description: "Task list for the Meeting-Room Bookings feature"
4	---
5	
6	# Tasks: Meeting-Room Bookings
7	
8	**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/001-room-bookings/`
9	
10	**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (gateway-http-api.md, service-messages.md, bookings-page.md), quickstart.md
11	
12	**Tests**: Included. FR-034 and Constitution Principle V (Test-First, non-negotiable) require them: every spec task is done first and MUST fail before the implementation task that follows it.
13	
14	**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story can be implemented and tested on its own.
15	
16	## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`
17	
18	- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
19	- **[Story]**: Which user story the task belongs to (US1–US4)
20	- Every task names the exact file it creates or edits
21	
22	## Path Conventions
23	
24	Nx monorepo, paths from the repository root: `libs/backend-common/src/lib/…`, `apps/gateway/src/booking/…`, `apps/booking/src/booking/…`, `apps/worker/src/confirmation/…`, `apps/web/src/…`. A spec sits next to its source file as `*.spec.ts` / `*.spec.tsx`.
25	
26	## Rules that apply to every task
27	
28	- Routes, patterns, DTO classes, error codes, header names, the queue name and constants are imported from `@roombook/contract`; nothing is added to or changed in `libs/contract`, `apps/room`, `apps/web/src/views/rooms`, `apps/web/src/pages/rooms` or `apps/web/src/services/room.service.ts` (FR-033).
29	- Errors are raised with `ExceptionHelper` from `@roombook/backend-common` and an `ErrorCodeEnum` value.
30	- No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object type as a parameter, explicit return type on every repository method, named imports only, kebab-case file names, every file under 200 lines, no narrative comments.
31	- Transactions only in repositories. No dependency is added. `.env` files are never read. Git stays local.
32	
33	## Assumptions made in this task list
34	
35	1. Specs are written for services, repositories, controllers, the guard, the interceptor, the processor, clients, utils, hooks and components. Modules, entities, migrations, `claim-booking-result.dto.ts` and `pages/bookings/index.tsx` get no spec of their own, as `room.module.ts`, `room.entity.ts`, the room migrations and `pages/rooms/index.tsx` have none today.
36	2. To keep User Story 1 testable on its own, its create path already writes the booking and the idempotency row in one transaction (the `CREATED` outcome) and the gateway interceptor already unwraps the booking. User Story 2 adds the key guard, the two advisory locks and the other three outcomes to the same files. Until User Story 2 is done, a create without a valid key or with a reused key is not answered as specified.
37	3. Error `message` texts are not fixed by the contract; the texts given in the tasks are the ones to use.
38	4. The simulated sender compares the address domain case-insensitively.
39	
40	---
41	
42	## Phase 1: Setup (Shared Infrastructure)
43	
44	**Purpose**: Confirm the starting point; the project, tooling and dependencies already exist.
45	
46	- [ ] T001 Run `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` from the repository root and confirm all three pass before any change; stop and report if one fails
47	
48	---
49	
50	## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)
51	
52	**Purpose**: Storage, the shared error guard and the two pure helpers every story builds on.
53	
54	**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.
55	
56	- [ ] T002 [P] Write the failing spec `libs/backend-common/src/lib/errors/error-response.guard.spec.ts`: `isErrorResponse` is true for `{ statusCode: number, errorCode: string, message: string }` and false for `null`, a string, and an object missing or mistyping any of the three fields
57	- [ ] T003 Create `libs/backend-common/src/lib/errors/error-response.guard.ts` exporting `isErrorResponse` (moved unchanged out of `rpc-exception.filter.ts`), import it in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/errors/rpc-exception.filter.ts`, and export it from `libs/backend-common/src/index.ts`; `rpc-exception.filter.spec.ts` must stay green
58	- [ ] T004 [P] Create `BookingEntity` (table `bookings`) in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/entities/booking.entity.ts` with: `id` `uuid` primary key `PK_bookings_id`, default `gen_random_uuid()`; `room_id` `uuid` not null, no foreign key; `title` `character varying(120)` not null; `organizer_email` `character varying(320)` not null; `starts_at` and `ends_at` `timestamp with time zone` not null; `confirmation_status` `character varying(10)` not null, default `PENDING`, typed `ConfirmationStatusEnum`; `confirmation_attempts` `integer` not null, default 0; `created_at` and `updated_at` `timestamp with time zone` not null, default `now()`; checks `CK_bookings_time_range` (`ends_at > starts_at`) and `CK_bookings_confirmation_status` (limits it to `PENDING`, `SENT`, `FAILED`); indexes `IDX_bookings_starts_at` on (`starts_at`, `id`) and `IDX_bookings_room_id_starts_at` on (`room_id`, `starts_at`, `id`); properties in camelCase
59	- [ ] T005 [P] Create `IdempotencyKeyEntity` (table `idempotency_keys`) in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/entities/idempotency-key.entity.ts` with: `key` `uuid` primary key `PK_idempotency_keys_key` (not generated); `request_fingerprint` `character(64)` not null; `response_status` `smallint` not null; `response_body` `jsonb` not null, typed `BookingDto`; `created_at` `timestamp with time zone` not null, default `now()`; no status column, no foreign key to `bookings`
60	- [ ] T006 [P] Create migration class `CreateBookings1731200000002` in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/database/migrations/1731200000002-create-bookings.ts`: `up` creates table `bookings` with exactly the columns, defaults, `PK_bookings_id`, `CK_bookings_time_range`, `CK_bookings_confirmation_status`, `IDX_bookings_starts_at` and `IDX_bookings_room_id_starts_at` listed in T004; `down` drops the table; follow the style of `1731200000000-create-rooms.ts`
61	- [ ] T007 [P] Create migration class `CreateIdempotencyKeys1731200000003` in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/database/migrations/1731200000003-create-idempotency-keys.ts`: `up` creates table `idempotency_keys` with exactly the columns and `PK_idempotency_keys_key` listed in T005; `down` drops the table
62	- [ ] T008 Register the new storage: add both migrations in timestamp order to `libs/backend-common/src/lib/database/migrations/index.ts`, add `BookingEntity` and `IdempotencyKeyEntity` to `entities` in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/database/data-source.ts`, and export both entities from `libs/backend-common/src/index.ts` (after T003, same file)
63	- [ ] T009 [P] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.mapper.spec.ts`: `toBookingDto(entity)` returns every `BookingDto` field in camelCase and answers `startsAt`, `endsAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt` with `toISOString()`
64	- [ ] T010 Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.mapper.ts` exporting `toBookingDto(entity: BookingEntity): BookingDto` so T009 passes
65	- [ ] T011 [P] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-time-range.util.spec.ts`: `parseBookingInstant` returns a `Date` for `2030-01-07T09:00:00.000Z` and `null` for a value that does not parse to an instant (for example the week date `2030-W02-1`); `isEndAfterStart` is true only when the end is strictly later, false when equal or earlier
66	- [ ] T012 Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-time-range.util.ts` exporting `parseBookingInstant(value: string): Date | null` (uses `new Date(value)`) and `isEndAfterStart(startsAt: Date, endsAt: Date): boolean` so T011 passes
67	
68	**Checkpoint**: `pnpm run build` and `pnpm run test` pass; user story work can begin.
69	
70	---
71	
72	## Phase 3: User Story 1 - Book a room and manage the booking (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP
73	
74	**Goal**: Five routes under `/api/bookings` on the gateway forward over NATS to the `booking` service, which validates, checks the room, stores, lists, reads, updates and deletes bookings.
75	
76	**Independent Test**: Through the gateway alone, create a booking for an existing room with a UUID `Idempotency-Key`, list it, read it, change its end time, delete it, and confirm that reading it afterwards answers 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` (quickstart scenarios 1 and 2).
77	
78	### Tests for User Story 1 (write first, must fail) ⚠️
79	
80	- [ ] T013 [P] [US1] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-fingerprint.util.spec.ts`: `bookingFingerprint` returns 64 lower-case hex characters, the same value for the same five field values whatever the property order, and a different value when any one of `roomId`, `title`, `organizerEmail`, `startsAt`, `endsAt` differs (including `2030-01-01T10:00:00Z` vs `2030-01-01T10:00:00.000Z`)
81	- [ ] T014 [P] [US1] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.spec.ts` with the TypeORM repository mocked (pattern of `apps/room/src/room/room.repository.spec.ts`): `findPage` orders by `startsAt` ASC then `id` ASC with `skip = (page - 1) * limit` and `take = limit`, and applies `roomId` to rows and total only when given; `findById` returns the entity or `null`; `updateIfTimeRangeValid` applies only the sent fields, sets `updated_at`, and returns `null` when no row matched; `deleteById` returns the deleted entity or `null`
82	- [ ] T015 [P] [US1] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.spec.ts` with the `DataSource` mocked: `claim(key, fingerprint, booking)` inserts the booking and the idempotency row (key, fingerprint, `response_status` 201, `response_body` the mapped `BookingDto`) inside one `dataSource.transaction` call and returns outcome `CREATED` with that `BookingDto`; an error on the second insert rejects so nothing is committed
83	- [ ] T016 [P] [US1] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/room.client.spec.ts` with the NATS `ClientProxy` mocked: `findRoomById` sends `RoomPatternEnum.FIND_BY_ID` with `{ id }` and returns the `RoomDto`; a plain `{ statusCode: 404, errorCode: 'NOT_FOUND.ROOM', message }` rejection is re-raised as an `RpcException` carrying the same object; an `RpcException` for 503 `UNAVAILABLE.SERVICE` passes through unchanged
84	- [ ] T017 [P] [US1] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.service.spec.ts` with `BookingRepository` mocked: `listBookings` returns `{ items, total, page, limit }` with mapped items; `findBookingById` returns the DTO or raises 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING`; `updateBooking` with no fields returns the stored booking unchanged without calling the update (404 when missing), raises 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` for a time that does not parse, returns the updated DTO, and when the repository update returns `null` raises 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` if the booking is missing or 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` if it exists; `deleteBooking` returns the deleted DTO or raises 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING`
85	- [ ] T018 [P] [US1] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/create-booking.service.spec.ts` with `RoomClient` and `IdempotentBookingRepository` mocked: a time that does not parse, or `endsAt` equal to or earlier than `startsAt`, raises 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` without asking the room service or claiming; a room error (404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM`, 503 `UNAVAILABLE.SERVICE`) propagates and nothing is claimed; a valid request claims with the lower-cased key and the fingerprint and returns `{ booking, replayed: false }`
86	- [ ] T019 [P] [US1] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.controller.spec.ts` with both services mocked: each of `BookingPatternEnum.CREATE`, `LIST`, `FIND_BY_ID`, `UPDATE` and `DELETE` delegates to one service method with the payload and returns its result
87	- [ ] T020 [P] [US1] Write the failing spec `apps/gateway/src/booking/idempotency-replay.interceptor.spec.ts`: for a handler result `{ booking, replayed: false }` the body becomes `booking` and no header is set; for `replayed: true` the body is `booking` and the response header `IDEMPOTENCY_REPLAYED_HEADER` is set to `true`
88	- [ ] T021 [P] [US1] Write the failing spec `apps/gateway/src/booking/booking.controller.spec.ts` (pattern of `apps/gateway/src/room/room.controller.spec.ts`, NATS client mocked): `POST` forwards `BookingPatternEnum.CREATE` with `{ idempotencyKey, booking }`; `GET` forwards `LIST` with the query; `GET :id` forwards `FIND_BY_ID` with `{ id }`; `PATCH :id` forwards `UPDATE` with `{ id, changes }`; `DELETE :id` forwards `DELETE` with `{ id }` and returns nothing
89	
90	### Implementation for User Story 1
91	
92	- [ ] T022 [P] [US1] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-fingerprint.util.ts` exporting `bookingFingerprint(booking: CreateBookingDto): string` — sha256 hex (`createHash` from `node:crypto`) of `JSON.stringify([roomId, title, organizerEmail, startsAt, endsAt])` (T013 passes)
93	- [ ] T023 [P] [US1] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/claim-booking-result.dto.ts` exporting `enum ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum { CREATED, REPLAYED, KEY_REUSED, IN_PROGRESS }` (string values equal to the names) and `class ClaimBookingResultDto { outcome: ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum; booking: BookingDto | null }`
94	- [ ] T024 [P] [US1] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.ts` with `findPage(query: ListBookingsQueryDto): Promise<[BookingEntity[], number]>`, `findById(id: string): Promise<BookingEntity | null>`, `updateIfTimeRangeValid(id: string, changes: UpdateBookingDto): Promise<BookingEntity | null>` (one conditional `UPDATE … RETURNING` that applies the sent fields and `updated_at = now()` only where the resulting `ends_at` is later than the resulting `starts_at`) and `deleteById(id: string): Promise<BookingEntity | null>` (one `DELETE … RETURNING`); no transaction (T014 passes)
95	- [ ] T025 [US1] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.ts` with `claim(key: string, fingerprint: string, booking: CreateBookingDto): Promise<ClaimBookingResultDto>`: in one `dataSource.transaction`, insert the booking, map it with `toBookingDto`, insert the `IdempotencyKeyEntity` row (`responseStatus` `HttpStatus.CREATED`, `responseBody` the DTO) and return outcome `CREATED` (T015 passes; depends on T010, T023)
96	- [ ] T026 [P] [US1] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/room.client.ts`: injectable `RoomClient` with `findRoomById(id: string): Promise<RoomDto>` using `NatsRequestUtil.send` on `NATS_CLIENT` with `RoomPatternEnum.FIND_BY_ID` and `RoomIdMessageDto`; a rejection for which `isErrorResponse` is true is re-raised as `new RpcException(error)`, any other error is rethrown (T016 passes)
97	- [ ] T027 [US1] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.service.ts` with `listBookings(query: ListBookingsQueryDto): Promise<PagedBookingsDto>`, `findBookingById(id: string): Promise<BookingDto>`, `updateBooking(message: UpdateBookingMessageDto): Promise<BookingDto>` and `deleteBooking(id: string): Promise<BookingDto>` as specified in T017; messages `Booking not found`, `startsAt and endsAt must be valid date-times`, `endsAt must be later than startsAt` (depends on T010, T012, T024)
98	- [ ] T028 [US1] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/create-booking.service.ts` with `createBooking(message: CreateBookingMessageDto): Promise<CreateBookingResultDto>`: lower-case the key, compute the fingerprint, check both times parse and `endsAt` is later than `startsAt` (else 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`), call `RoomClient.findRoomById(booking.roomId)`, call `IdempotentBookingRepository.claim`, return `{ booking, replayed: false }` (T018 passes; depends on T012, T022, T025, T026)
99	- [ ] T029 [US1] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.controller.ts` with one `@MessagePattern` handler per pattern `BookingPatternEnum.CREATE` (`CreateBookingMessageDto` → `CreateBookingResultDto`), `LIST` (`ListBookingsQueryDto` → `PagedBookingsDto`), `FIND_BY_ID`, `UPDATE` (`UpdateBookingMessageDto`) and `DELETE` (`BookingIdMessageDto` → the deleted `BookingDto`), each a single delegating statement (T019 passes)
100	- [ ] T030 [US1] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.module.ts` (`TypeOrmModule.forFeature([BookingEntity, IdempotencyKeyEntity])`, controller `BookingController`, providers `BookingService`, `CreateBookingService`, `BookingRepository`, `IdempotentBookingRepository`, `RoomClient`) and edit `apps/booking/src/app/app.module.ts` to import `NatsClientModule` and `BookingModule`
101	- [ ] T031 [P] [US1] Create `apps/gateway/src/booking/idempotency-replay.interceptor.ts`: `IdempotencyReplayInterceptor` maps the handler's `CreateBookingResultDto` to `result.booking` and sets the response header `IDEMPOTENCY_REPLAYED_HEADER` to `true` only when `result.replayed` is true (T020 passes)
102	- [ ] T032 [US1] Create `apps/gateway/src/booking/booking.controller.ts` on `@Controller(ApiRouteEnum.BOOKINGS)`, each handler one `NatsRequestUtil.send` statement: `POST` (`@UseInterceptors(IdempotencyReplayInterceptor)`, `@Headers(IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_HEADER)` key and `@Body() CreateBookingDto`, answers 201); `GET` with `@Query() ListBookingsQueryDto`; `GET :id`, `PATCH :id` and `DELETE :id` with `@Param('id', ParseUUIDPipe)`; `PATCH` body `UpdateBookingDto` through a handler-level `new ValidationPipe({ transform: true, whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true })`; `DELETE` with `@HttpCode(204)` returning `Promise<void>` (T021 passes; depends on T031)
103	- [ ] T033 [US1] Create `apps/gateway/src/booking/booking.module.ts` (controller `BookingController`, provider `IdempotencyReplayInterceptor`) and edit `apps/gateway/src/app/app.module.ts` to import `BookingModule`
104	
105	**Checkpoint**: `pnpm run test` passes; quickstart scenarios 1 and 2 pass against the running stack. A booking stays `PENDING` with 0 attempts until User Story 3.
106	
107	---
108	
109	## Phase 4: User Story 2 - Retry a create safely (Priority: P2)
110	
111	**Goal**: The `Idempotency-Key` is required and checked before the body; the same key and body replay the stored answer; a different body answers 422; a create in progress answers 409; two simultaneous creates never store two bookings.
112	
113	**Independent Test**: Send the same create twice with one key and observe one booking and an identical second answer with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`; then vary the body, the key and the timing to observe 400, 422 and 409 (quickstart scenarios 3–6).
114	
115	### Tests for User Story 2 (write first, must fail) ⚠️
116	
117	- [ ] T034 [P] [US2] Write the failing spec `apps/gateway/src/booking/idempotency-key.guard.spec.ts`: a request whose `idempotency-key` header is a UUID is allowed; a missing header and the value `abc` raise 400 `BAD_REQUEST.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY` (`ErrorCodeEnum.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID`)

# Tasks: Meeting-Room Bookings

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/001-room-bookings/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (gateway-http-api.md, service-messages.md, bookings-page.md), quickstart.md

**Tests**: Included. FR-034 and Constitution Principle V (Test-First, non-negotiable) require them: every spec task is done first and MUST fail before the implementation task that follows it.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story can be implemented and tested on its own.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: Which user story the task belongs to (US1–US4)
- Every task names the exact file it creates or edits

## Path Conventions

Nx monorepo, paths from the repository root: `libs/backend-common/src/lib/…`, `apps/gateway/src/booking/…`, `apps/booking/src/booking/…`, `apps/worker/src/confirmation/…`, `apps/web/src/…`. A spec sits next to its source file as `*.spec.ts` / `*.spec.tsx`.

## Rules that apply to every task

- Routes, patterns, DTO classes, error codes, header names, the queue name and constants are imported from `@roombook/contract`; nothing is added to or changed in `libs/contract`, `apps/room`, `apps/web/src/views/rooms`, `apps/web/src/pages/rooms` or `apps/web/src/services/room.service.ts` (FR-033).
- Errors are raised with `ExceptionHelper` from `@roombook/backend-common` and an `ErrorCodeEnum` value.
- No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object type as a parameter, explicit return type on every repository method, named imports only, kebab-case file names, every file under 200 lines, no narrative comments.
- Transactions only in repositories. No dependency is added. `.env` files are never read. Git stays local.

## Assumptions made in this task list

1. Specs are written for services, repositories, controllers, the guard, the interceptor, the processor, clients, utils, hooks and components. Modules, entities, migrations, `claim-booking-result.dto.ts` and `pages/bookings/index.tsx` get no spec of their own, as `room.module.ts`, `room.entity.ts`, the room migrations and `pages/rooms/index.tsx` have none today.
2. To keep User Story 1 testable on its own, its create path already writes the booking and the idempotency row in one transaction (the `CREATED` outcome) and the gateway interceptor already unwraps the booking. User Story 2 adds the key guard, the two advisory locks and the other three outcomes to the same files. Until User Story 2 is done, a create without a valid key or with a reused key is not answered as specified.
3. Error `message` texts are not fixed by the contract; the texts given in the tasks are the ones to use.
4. The simulated sender compares the address domain case-insensitively.

---

- [ ] T039 [US2] Add `@UseGuards(IdempotencyKeyGuard)` to the `POST` handler in `apps/gateway/src/booking/booking.controller.ts` and register the guard as a provider in `apps/gateway/src/booking/booking.module.ts` (T035 passes)

---

## Phase 5: User Story 3 - Get a confirmation (Priority: P3)

**Goal**: Each created booking gets exactly one job on `booking-confirmation`; the worker runs the simulated sender and reports every attempt over NATS; the `booking` service records the outcome idempotently.

**Independent Test**: Create three bookings with organizer addresses in an ordinary domain, `@retry.example` and `@bounce.example`; after 10 seconds they read `SENT`/1, `SENT`/3 and `FAILED`/3 (quickstart scenarios 7–9).

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: none.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: after Setup; blocks every story.
- **US1 (Phase 3)**: after Foundational.
- **US2 (Phase 4)**: after US1 — it extends `idempotent-booking.repository.ts`, `create-booking.service.ts` and the gateway controller created there.
- **US3 (Phase 5)**: after US1 (it extends the `booking` service files and needs created bookings). Independent of US2 in code, but both edit `create-booking.service.ts` and its spec, so do them one after the other (US2 first).
- **US4 (Phase 6)**: code and unit tests depend only on Foundational being merged (the page talks to mocked services); the manual check (T091) needs US1–US3 running.
- **Polish (Phase 7)**: after every story.

### User Story Dependencies

```text
Setup → Foundational → US1 → US2 → US3 → Polish
                    └──────── US4 ──────────┘   (US4 can run in parallel with US1–US3)
```

### Within Each User Story

- Spec task first; it must fail for the right reason before its implementation task starts.
- Utils and DTOs → repositories → clients → services → controllers → module wiring.
- A task marked "Extend" edits a file created earlier and is never parallel with another task on that file.

9	## Summary
10	
11	Add bookings to roombook in four parts, all on the existing stack and the existing shared contract:
12	
13	1. **Bookings API** — five routes under `/api/bookings` on the gateway, which validates and forwards
14	   over NATS; the `booking` service owns the rules and two new tables.
15	2. **Idempotent create** — the key is checked by a gateway guard; the `booking` repository claims the
16	   key and inserts the booking in one transaction, using two transaction-scoped advisory locks to
17	   answer "in progress" (409) and "key reused" (422) without a stored in-progress state.
18	3. **Confirmation job** — the `booking` service enqueues one BullMQ job per created booking; the
19	   `worker` reads the booking over NATS, runs a simulated sender and reports each attempt; the
20	   `booking` service records it with one conditional update.
21	4. **Bookings page** — `/bookings` in `apps/web` with a table, room filter, create form, edit and
22	   delete dialogs, and an idempotency key that survives only a network error.

46	## Constitution Check

50	Evaluated against `.specify/memory/constitution.md` v1.0.0.
51	
52	| Principle | Gate | Result |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| I. Contract as Source of Truth | Routes, patterns, queue name, DTO classes, error codes, header names and constants all come from `@roombook/contract`. Where the contract defines no answer class (`deleteBooking`, `recordConfirmationResult`) or no job name, an existing contract export is reused; nothing is added to or changed in the contract. Errors cross boundaries as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }` through `ExceptionHelper`. | PASS |
55	| II. Layered Architecture | Gateway handlers are one forwarding statement each, following the existing `RoomController`; the key check is a guard and the replay header an interceptor. `POST` takes `CreateBookingDto`, `PATCH` takes `UpdateBookingDto`. # Implementation Plan: Meeting-Room Bookings

**Branch**: none — no branch hook is installed; the work stays on `main` (feature directory `specs/001-room-bookings`) | **Date**: 2026-11-10 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-room-bookings/spec.md`

**Note**: This template is filled in by the `/speckit-plan` command; its definition describes the execution workflow.

## Summary

Add bookings to roombook in four parts, all on the existing stack and the existing shared contract:

1. **Bookings API** — five routes under `/api/bookings` on the gateway, which validates and forwards
   over NATS; the `booking` service owns the rules and two new tables.
2. **Idempotent create** — the key is checked by a gateway guard; the `booking` repository claims the
   key and inserts the booking in one transaction, using two transaction-scoped advisory locks to
   answer "in progress" (409) and "key reused" (422) without a stored in-progress state.
3. **Confirmation job** — the `booking` service enqueues one BullMQ job per created booking; the
   `worker` reads the booking over NATS, runs a simulated sender and reports each attempt; the
   `booking` service records it with one conditional update.
4. **Bookings page** — `/bookings` in `apps/web` with a table, room filter, create form, edit and
   delete dialogs, and an idempotency key that survives only a network error.

Design decisions and their reasons are in [research.md](./research.md).

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.9 on Node 22 or newer

**Primary Dependencies**: NestJS 11 (HTTP gateway, NATS microservices), TypeORM 0.3, BullMQ 5 with `@nestjs/bullmq`, class-validator / class-transformer, Next.js 15 (pages router) with React 18 and MUI 5, react-hook-form with yup, axios, uuid — all already installed; no dependency is added

**Storage**: PostgreSQL 15 (two new tables: `bookings`, `idempotency_keys`); Redis 7.2 for the `booking-confirmation` queue

**Testing**: Jest 29 through Nx (`pnpm run test`); `@nestjs/testing` with mocked neighbours for the backend, Testing Library with the service layer mocked for the web page

**Target Platform**: Node services and a browser frontend, run locally through `pnpm run stack:up` (Docker for Postgres, Redis and NATS)

**Project Type**: Web application in an Nx monorepo — HTTP gateway, NATS services, queue worker, Next.js frontend

**Performance Goals**: every booking reaches its final confirmation state within 10 seconds of creation (SC-004); no throughput target

**Constraints**: `libs/contract`, `apps/room` and the `/rooms` page are not changed (FR-033); no new dependency; the worker has no database access; transactions only in repositories; every code file under 200 lines; `.env` files are never read

**Scale/Scope**: a demo system with synthetic data and no sign-in; 5 HTTP routes, 6 NATS handlers, 1 queue, 2 tables, 1 page; about 45 new source files (specs included) across `apps/gateway`, `apps/booking`, `apps/worker`, `apps/web` and `libs/backend-common`

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

| I. Contract as Source of Truth | Routes, patterns, queue name, DTO classes, error codes, header names and constants all come from `@roombook/contract`. Where the contract defines no answer class (`deleteBooking`, `recordConfirmationResult`) or no job name, an existing contract export is reused; nothing is added to or changed in the contract. Errors cross boundaries as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }` through `ExceptionHelper`. | PASS |
| II. Layered Architecture | Gateway handlers are one forwarding statement each, following the existing `RoomController`; the key check is a guard and the replay header an interceptor. `POST` takes `CreateBookingDto`, `PATCH` takes `UpdateBookingDto`. Rules live in `booking` services, data access in repositories, and the only transaction is in `IdempotentBookingRepository`. The gateway and the worker have no database access. Each new class is registered in one module. No literal port, host, URL or secret is added; no new environment variable is needed. Health patterns for all services already exist and no deployable is added. | PASS |
| III. Strict TypeScript | No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object parameter types, explicit return types on every repository method, named imports only. Internal shapes (claim result, sender decision) are named classes or `type`s. | PASS |
| IV. Small, Self-Describing Files | Kebab-case names that state their purpose; the booking create flow, the other booking operations, the two repositories and the page's parts are split so each file stays under 200 lines; no narrative comments. | PASS |
| V. Test-First | Every new or modified service, repository, controller, guard, interceptor, processor, hook and component gets a `*.spec.ts(x)` next to it, written and failing before the implementation. | PASS |
| Safety Constraints | `.env` files are not read (configuration is referred to by name); git stays local; no dependency is added. | PASS |
| Quality Gates | `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` are the completion check (quickstart, "Automated gates"). | PASS |

  repository; the service still decides the answer and its error code (Principle II).

  frozen area, and keeps the filter's behaviour (its spec stays green).

22	
23	These rules apply to every change in this repository.
24	
25	## Core Principles
26	
27	### I. Contract as Source of Truth
28	
29	- `libs/contract` (`@roombook/contract`) is the source of truth for routes, message patterns,
30	  queue names, DTO classes, error codes and job payloads.
31	- Code MUST use what `@roombook/contract` exports. A route, pattern, field or error code
32	  MUST NOT be invented outside it.
33	- Errors MUST cross service boundaries as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`, with
34	  `errorCode` taken from `ErrorCodeEnum`.
35	
36	Rationale: the gateway, the NATS services, the worker and the frontend stay compatible only
37	when they all read the same definitions.
38	
39	### II. Layered Architecture
40	
41	- Controllers MUST be thin: at most five statements, all delegating to a service. Controllers
42	  MUST NOT contain logic.
43	- Every POST, PUT and PATCH handler MUST take a DTO class with class-validator decorators as
44	  its body.
45	- Services hold business rules and MUST delegate data access to repositories.
46	- Database transactions MUST live in repositories only, never in services.
47	- The gateway MUST NOT hold database access or business rules; it validates input and forwards
48	  over NATS.
49	- Every controller, service and provider MUST be registered in exactly one module.
50	- Source files MUST NOT contain literal ports, hosts, URLs or secrets; configuration comes from
51	  environment variables read through the config module.
52	- Every deployable service MUST have a health endpoint: a health message pattern on each NATS
53	  service, exposed by the gateway as `GET /api/health/<service>`.
54	
55	Rationale: each layer has one responsibility, so a rule has one place to live and one place
56	to be tested.
57	
58	### III. Strict TypeScript
59	
60	- `interface` MUST NOT be used; use `class` for DTOs and `type` for everything else.
61	- `any` MUST NOT be used.
62	- An inline object type MUST NOT be used as a function parameter; define a named DTO class.
63	- Every repository method MUST have an explicit return type.
64	- Imports MUST be named imports; `import * as` MUST NOT be used.

# roombook Constitution

These rules apply to every change in this repository.

## Core Principles

### I. Contract as Source of Truth

- `libs/contract` (`@roombook/contract`) is the source of truth for routes, message patterns,
  queue names, DTO classes, error codes and job payloads.
- Code MUST use what `@roombook/contract` exports. A route, pattern, field or error code
  MUST NOT be invented outside it.
- Errors MUST cross service boundaries as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`, with
  `errorCode` taken from `ErrorCodeEnum`.

Rationale: the gateway, the NATS services, the worker and the frontend stay compatible only
when they all read the same definitions.

### II. Layered Architecture

- Controllers MUST be thin: at most five statements, all delegating to a service. Controllers
  MUST NOT contain logic.
- Every POST, PUT and PATCH handler MUST take a DTO class with class-validator decorators as
  its body.
- Services hold business rules and MUST delegate data access to repositories.
- Database transactions MUST live in repositories only, never in services.
- The gateway MUST NOT hold database access or business rules; it validates input and forwards
  over NATS.
- Every controller, service and provider MUST be registered in exactly one module.
- Source files MUST NOT contain literal ports, hosts, URLs or secrets; configuration comes from
  environment variables read through the config module.
- Every deployable service MUST have a health endpoint: a health message pattern on each NATS
  service, exposed by the gateway as `GET /api/health/<service>`.

Rationale: each layer has one responsibility, so a rule has one place to live and one place
to be tested.

### III. Strict TypeScript

- `interface` MUST NOT be used; use `class` for DTOs and `type` for everything else.
- `any` MUST NOT be used.
- An inline object type MUST NOT be used as a function parameter; define a named DTO class.
- Every repository method MUST have an explicit return type.
- Imports MUST be named imports; `import * as` MUST NOT be used.

Rationale: explicit, named types keep the contract visible at every boundary and stop
untyped data from leaking between layers.

### IV. Small, Self-Describing Files

- File names MUST be kebab-case and describe their purpose.
- Every code file MUST stay under 200 lines; split by concern.
- Comments MUST NOT restate what the code does. A comment is allowed only for a non-obvious
  constraint, in one short line.

Rationale: a file whose name and size reveal its purpose can be found and understood without
opening its neighbours.

### V. Test-First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

- Every new or modified service MUST have at least one unit test in a `*.spec.ts` file next
  to it.
- The failing test MUST be written before the implementation.

Rationale: a test written first proves the behaviour was missing and that the change added it.

## Safety Constraints

- `.env` and `.env.*` files MUST NOT be read; refer to configuration by variable name.
- Git is local only: no remote, no push, no pull request.
- Dependencies MUST NOT be added.

## Quality Gates

A change is finished only when all three commands pass:

- `pnpm run build`
- `pnpm run lint`
- `pnpm run test`

## Governance

- This constitution supersedes any other practice in this repository. Where another document
  conflicts with it, the constitution wins.
- Amendments are made by editing this file through `/speckit-constitution`, with the change
  recorded in a local commit.
- Versions follow semantic versioning: MAJOR for removing or redefining a principle, MINOR for
  adding a principle or section or materially expanding guidance, PATCH for clarifications and
  wording.
- Every specification, plan, task list and implementation MUST be checked against these
  principles. A violation MUST be fixed, or justified in writing in the plan, before the
  change is considered finished.

**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-11-10 | **Last Amended**: 2026-11-10

# Tasks: Meeting-Room Bookings

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/001-room-bookings/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (gateway-http-api.md, service-messages.md, bookings-page.md), quickstart.md

**Tests**: Included. FR-034 and Constitution Principle V (Test-First, non-negotiable) require them: every spec task is done first and MUST fail before the implementation task that follows it.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story can be implemented and tested on its own.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: Which user story the task belongs to (US1–US4)
- Every task names the exact file it creates or edits

## Path Conventions

Nx monorepo, paths from the repository root: `libs/backend-common/src/lib/…`, `apps/gateway/src/booking/…`, `apps/booking/src/booking/…`, `apps/worker/src/confirmation/…`, `apps/web/src/…`. A spec sits next to its source file as `*.spec.ts` / `*.spec.tsx`.

## Rules that apply to every task

- Routes, patterns, DTO classes, error codes, header names, the queue name and constants are imported from `@roombook/contract`; nothing is added to or changed in `libs/contract`, `apps/room`, `apps/web/src/views/rooms`, `apps/web/src/pages/rooms` or `apps/web/src/services/room.service.ts` (FR-033).
- Errors are raised with `ExceptionHelper` from `@roombook/backend-common` and an `ErrorCodeEnum` value.
- No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object type as a parameter, explicit return type on every repository method, named imports only, kebab-case file names, every file under 200 lines, no narrative comments.
- Transactions only in repositories. No dependency is added. `.env` files are never read. Git stays local.

## Assumptions made in this task list

1. Specs are written for services, repositories, controllers, the guard, the interceptor, the processor, clients, utils, hooks and components. Modules, entities, migrations, `claim-booking-result.dto.ts` and `pages/bookings/index.tsx` get no spec of their own, as `room.module.ts`, `room.entity.ts`, the room migrations and `pages/rooms/index.tsx` have none today.
2. To keep User Story 1 testable on its own, its create path already writes the booking and the idempotency row in one transaction (the `CREATED` outcome) and the gateway interceptor already unwraps the booking. User Story 2 adds the key guard, the two advisory locks and the other three outcomes to the same files. Until User Story 2 is done, a create without a valid key or with a reused key is not answered as specified.
3. Error `message` texts are not fixed by the contract; the texts given in the tasks are the ones to use.
4. The simulated sender compares the address domain case-insensitively.

---

## Phase 1: Setup (Shared Infrastructure)

**Purpose**: Confirm the starting point; the project, tooling and dependencies already exist.

- [ ] T001 Run `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` from the repository root and confirm all three pass before any change; stop and report if one fails

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: Storage, the shared error guard and the two pure helpers every story builds on.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: none.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: after Setup; blocks every story.
- **US1 (Phase 3)**: after Foundational.
- **US2 (Phase 4)**: after US1 — it extends `idempotent-booking.repository.ts`, `create-booking.service.ts` and the gateway controller created there.
- **US3 (Phase 5)**: after US1 (it extends the `booking` service files and needs created bookings). Independent of US2 in code, but both edit `create-booking.service.ts` and its spec, so do them one after the other (US2 first).
- **US4 (Phase 6)**: code and unit tests depend only on Foundational being merged (the page talks to mocked services); the manual check (T091) needs US1–US3 running.
- **Polish (Phase 7)**: after every story.

### User Story Dependencies

```text
Setup → Foundational → US1 → US2 → US3 → Polish
                    └──────── US4 ──────────┘   (US4 can run in parallel with US1–US3)
```

### Within Each User Story

- Spec task first; it must fail for the right reason before its implementation task starts.
- Utils and DTOs → repositories → clients → services → controllers → module wiring.
- A task marked "Extend" edits a file created earlier and is never parallel with another task on that file.

### Parallel Opportunities

- Foundational: T002, T004–T007, T009 and T011 together; T003 → T008 in order (both edit `libs/backend-common/src/index.ts`).
- US1: all spec tasks T013–T021 together; then T022, T023, T024, T026 and T031 together.
- US2: T034 with T036/T037; T038 alongside T040.
- US3: T042, T047–T050 together; T051, T057 and T058 together; the worker tasks (T057–T061) alongside the `booking` service tasks (T051–T056).
- US4: all spec tasks T062–T073 together; then T074–T077, T080, T085 and T086 together.
- US4 as a whole alongside US1–US3 when a second developer is available.

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Phase 1: Setup (T001).
2. Phase 2: Foundational (T002–T012).
3. Phase 3: User Story 1 (T013–T033).
4. **Stop and validate**: `pnpm run test`, then quickstart scenarios 1 and 2 with a UUID `Idempotency-Key`.

### Incremental Delivery

1. Setup + Foundational → storage and helpers ready.
2. US1 → bookings API works end to end (MVP).
3. US2 → create is safe to retry (quickstart 3–6).
4. US3 → confirmations run (quickstart 7–9).
5. US4 → the page (quickstart 10).
6. Polish → gates, scope check, full quickstart.

### Parallel Team Strategy

1. Everyone: Setup + Foundational.
2. Developer A: US1 → US2 → US3 (backend, same files in sequence).
3. Developer B: US4 (frontend, mocked service layer), then joins the quickstart run.

2

6	
7	**Note**: This template is filled in by the `/speckit-plan` command; its definition describes the execution workflow.
8	
9	## Summary
10	
11	Add bookings to roombook in four parts, all on the existing stack and the existing shared contract:
12	
13	1. **Bookings API** — five routes under `/api/bookings` on the gateway, which validates and forwards
14	   over NATS; the `booking` service owns the rules and two new tables.
15	2. **Idempotent create** — the key is checked by a gateway guard; the `booking` repository claims the
16	   key and inserts the booking in one transaction, using two transaction-scoped advisory locks to
17	   answer "in progress" (409) and "key reused" (422) without a stored in-progress state.
18	3. **Confirmation job** — the `booking` service enqueues one BullMQ job per created booking; the
19	   `worker` reads the booking over NATS, runs a simulated sender and reports each attempt; the
20	   `booking` service records it with one conditional update.
21	4. **Bookings page** — `/bookings` in `apps/web` with a table, room filter, create form, edit and
22	   delete dialogs, and an idempotency key that survives only a network error.
23	
24	Design decisions and their reasons are in [research.md](./research.md).
25	
26	## Technical Context
27	
28	**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.9 on Node 22 or newer
29	
30	**Primary Dependencies**: NestJS 11 (HTTP gateway, NATS microservices), TypeORM 0.3, BullMQ 5 with `@nestjs/bullmq`, class-validator / class-transformer, Next.js 15 (pages router) with React 18 and MUI 5, react-hook-form with yup, axios, uuid — all already installed; no dependency is added
31	
32	**Storage**: PostgreSQL 15 (two new tables: `bookings`, `idempotency_keys`); Redis 7.2 for the `booking-confirmation` queue
33	
34	**Testing**: Jest 29 through Nx (`pnpm run test`); `@nestjs/testing` with mocked neighbours for the backend, Testing Library with the service layer mocked for the web page
35	
36	**Target Platform**: Node services and a browser frontend, run locally through `pnpm run stack:up` (Docker for Postgres, Redis and NATS)
37	
38	**Project Type**: Web application in an Nx monorepo — HTTP gateway, NATS services, queue worker, Next.js frontend
39	
40	**Performance Goals**: every booking reaches its final confirmation state within 10 seconds of creation (SC-004); no throughput target
41	
42	**Constraints**: `libs/contract`, `apps/room` and the `/rooms` page are not changed (FR-033); no new dependency; the worker has no database access; transactions only in repositories; every code file under 200 lines; `.env` files are never read
43	
44	**Scale/Scope**: a demo system with synthetic data and no sign-in; 5 HTTP routes, 6 NATS handlers, 1 queue, 2 tables, 1 page; about 45 new source files (specs included) across `apps/gateway`, `apps/booking`, `apps/worker`, `apps/web` and `libs/backend-common`

52	| Principle | Gate | Result |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| I. Contract as Source of Truth | Routes, patterns, queue name, DTO classes, error codes, header names and constants all come from `@roombook/contract`. Where the contract defines no answer class (`deleteBooking`, `recordConfirmationResult`) or no job name, an existing contract export is reused; nothing is added to or changed in the contract. Errors cross boundaries as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }` through `ExceptionHelper`. | PASS |
55	| II. Layered Architecture | Gateway handlers are one forwarding statement each, following the existing `RoomController`; the key check is a guard and the replay header an interceptor. `POST` takes `CreateBookingDto`, `PATCH` takes `UpdateBookingDto`. Rules live in `booking` services, data access in repositories, and the only transaction is in `IdempotentBookingRepository`. The gateway and the worker have no database access. Each new class is registered in one module. No literal port, host, URL or secret is added; no new environment variable is needed. Health patterns for all services already exist and no deployable is added. | PASS |
56	| III. Strict TypeScript | No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object parameter types, explicit return types on every repository method, named imports only. Internal shapes (claim result, sender decision) are named classes or `type`s. | PASS |
57	| IV. Small, Self-Describing Files | Kebab-case names that state their purpose; the booking create flow, the other booking operations, the two repositories and the page's parts are split so each file stays under 200 lines; no narrative comments. | PASS |
58	| V. Test-First | Every new or modified service, repository, controller, guard, interceptor, processor, hook and component gets a `*.spec.ts(x)` next to it, written and failing before the implementation. | PASS |
59	| Safety Constraints | `.env` files are not read (configuration is referred to by name); git stays local; no dependency is added. | PASS |
60	| Quality Gates | `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` are the completion check (quickstart, "Automated gates"). | PASS |

199	   the room is being checked are answered as create plus replay (or 409), which the spec allows.
200	2. The idempotency table has no status column; a row exists only for a completed create.
201	3. Bodies are "the same" when the five values are the same strings; the key is compared
202	   case-insensitively.
203	4. A replay is always answered 201, the only status ever stored.
204	5. Any unknown field on `PATCH` answers 400; unknown fields on `POST` are dropped.

206	   offset.

210	9. The BullMQ job name is the queue name.
211	10. The enqueue call is bounded at 2 seconds; that limit is a code constant, not configuration.
212	11. Concurrency (SC-002) is proven against the running stack in the quickstart; unit tests cover each
213	    claim outcome with the database mocked, as the existing repository specs do.
214	12. The page's table has a fixed page size of 10 and reloads the list after each change.

1	# Research: Meeting-Room Bookings
2	
3	**Feature**: `specs/001-room-bookings` | **Date**: 2026-11-10
4	
5	The Technical Context had no open `NEEDS CLARIFICATION` after reading the repository: the stack, the
6	contract and the test tooling are all fixed by the existing code. The decisions below settle the design
7	questions the specification leaves to the plan. Facts marked *(verified)* were checked in this
8	repository's source or in the installed packages under `node_modules`; everything else is a design
9	choice or a stated assumption.
10	
11	## R1. Where the idempotency key is validated
12	
13	- **Decision**: A gateway guard (`IdempotencyKeyGuard`) on `POST /api/bookings` checks the
14	  `Idempotency-Key` header with `isUUID` from `class-validator` and raises
15	  `ExceptionHelper.badRequest(ErrorCodeEnum.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID, …)`.
16	- **Rationale**: The spec requires the key to be checked before the body. Guards run before pipes
17	  *(verified: `router-execution-context.js` calls `fnCanActivate` before the handler's pipes)*. A header
18	  pipe would not give that order: parameter pipes are resolved with `Promise.all` *(verified, same
19	  file)*, so the first rejection is not deterministic. The existing `RpcExceptionFilter` already turns
20	  the raised `RpcException` into `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`.
21	- **Alternatives considered**: a pipe on `@Headers()` (order not guaranteed); validating in the
22	  `booking` service (the gateway is the layer that validates input, and a body error would win).
23	
24	## R2. How the replay header is set while the controller stays thin
25	
26	- **Decision**: A gateway interceptor (`IdempotencyReplayInterceptor`) receives the
27	  `CreateBookingResultDto` from the handler, sets `Idempotency-Replayed: true` when `replayed` is true
28	  and returns `result.booking` as the body. The handler is a single forwarding statement.
29	- **Rationale**: The contract's NATS answer is `{ booking, replayed }` but the HTTP body is the booking
30	  alone. Mapping it in an interceptor keeps the controller within the five-statement rule and keeps
31	  header handling out of the service layer.
32	- **Alternatives considered**: `@Res({ passthrough: true })` in the handler (puts branching in the
33	  controller).
34	
35	## R3. Idempotent create: one transaction, in-progress and reuse detection
36	
37	- **Decision**: The `booking` repository runs the whole claim in one transaction:
38	  1. `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('<key>:<fingerprint>', 0))` — not obtained means the
39	     same key with the same body is being processed now → outcome `IN_PROGRESS` (409).
40	  2. `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('<key>', 0))` — not obtained means the key is being
41	     processed with a different body → outcome `KEY_REUSED` (422).
42	  3. Read the idempotency row for the key. Present with the same fingerprint → `REPLAYED` with the
43	     stored body; present with another fingerprint → `KEY_REUSED`.
44	  4. Otherwise insert the booking and the idempotency row (key, fingerprint, response status 201,
45	     response body) → `CREATED`.
46	
47	  The service maps the outcome to the answer; the repository holds no error codes.
48	- **Rationale**:
49	  - FR-013 requires claiming the key and inserting the booking in one transaction. Both writes and the
50	    locks live in one transaction, so a failed or crashed request leaves no row and no lock: the key
51	    stays usable, with no clean-up job.
52	  - FR-016 needs a real "in progress" answer. A row inserted by an open transaction is invisible to
53	    other transactions, and a plain conflicting insert would wait instead of answering. A try-lock
54	    answers immediately.
55	  - The edge case "same key, different body, first request still in progress → 422" needs the body to
56	    be distinguishable without reading the uncommitted row. Two locks do that: the holder of the key
57	    lock always also holds the lock for its own fingerprint, so a request that obtained its own
58	    fingerprint lock but not the key lock necessarily has a different body.
59	  - FR-017: the key lock plus the primary key on the idempotency table make two bookings for one key
60	    impossible.
61	  - Transaction-scoped advisory locks are released at commit or rollback, so nothing is left to
62	    release by hand. `hashtextextended` exists from PostgreSQL 11; the stack runs PostgreSQL 15
63	    *(verified: `docker-compose.yml`)*.
64	- **Consequences to know**:
65	  - "In progress" is the open claim transaction, not a stored status. The idempotency table therefore
66	    has no status column; a row exists only for a completed request.
67	  - The room check happens before the transaction (R4). Two same-key requests that overlap only during
68	    their room checks are both answered correctly (one creates, the other replays or gets 409), which
69	    is what acceptance scenario US2-7 allows.
70	  - A 64-bit hash collision between two different keys could cause a spurious 409 or 422 for a request
71	    that would otherwise succeed; it can never cause a duplicate booking. Accepted.
72	- **Alternatives considered**:
73	  - A committed `IN_PROGRESS` row written before the booking: makes in-progress and body mismatch
74	    trivially visible, but breaks "one transaction" and leaves a stuck key forever after a crash,
75	    because keys never expire.
76	  - `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` alone: the second request blocks until the first commits and
77	    then replays; 409 would never be answered.
78	  - `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` and catching the timeout error: works, but uses an error as control flow
79	    and cannot tell a same-body from a different-body request.
80	
81	## R4. Order of checks on create
82	
83	- **Decision**:
84	  1. Gateway guard: idempotency key → 400 `BAD_REQUEST.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`.
85	  2. Gateway validation pipe: body → 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`.
86	  3. `booking` service: plain read of the idempotency row. Same fingerprint → replay; other
87	     fingerprint → 422.
88	  4. `booking` service: times form valid instants and `endsAt` is later than `startsAt` → else 400.
89	  5. `booking` service asks the `room` service → 404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` or 503 `UNAVAILABLE.SERVICE`.
90	  6. Repository claim transaction (R3).
91	  7. Enqueue the confirmation job (R6) — only for outcome `CREATED`.
92	- **Rationale**: Steps 4 and 5 store nothing, so FR-018 holds without any clean-up. Step 3 lets a
93	  replay be answered from the stored response even when the `room` service is down, and without a
94	  needless NATS call; step 6 repeats the same check under the lock, which is what makes it safe.
95	- **Alternatives considered**: doing the room check inside the transaction (a transaction would stay
96	  open across a NATS call of up to 5 seconds, and the transaction must stay inside the repository).
97	
98	## R5. Request fingerprint and "same body"
99	
100	- **Decision**: `sha256` (Node's built-in `crypto`) over
101	  `JSON.stringify([roomId, title, organizerEmail, startsAt, endsAt])`, stored as 64 hex characters.
102	  The key is lower-cased before it is used for locks and storage.
103	- **Rationale**: A fixed field order makes JSON field order and whitespace irrelevant, as the spec
104	  assumes. Unknown fields are already removed by the gateway's `whitelist: true`.
105	- **Assumption**: values are compared as the strings the client sent. `2030-01-01T10:00:00Z` and
106	  `2030-01-01T10:00:00.000Z` are the same instant but different bodies (422). A retry resends the same
107	  bytes, so this does not affect the intended use.
108	- **Alternatives considered**: normalising times to instants before hashing (more rules to explain,
109	  no benefit for a retry).
110	
111	## R6. Enqueueing the confirmation job
112	
113	- **Decision**: After the claim transaction commits with outcome `CREATED`, a
114	  `ConfirmationQueueProducer` calls `queue.add(QueueEnum.BOOKING_CONFIRMATION, { bookingId }, { jobId:
115	  confirmationJobId(bookingId), attempts: CONFIRMATION_JOB_ATTEMPTS, backoff: { type: 'exponential',
116	  delay: CONFIRMATION_BACKOFF_MS } })`. The call is bounded by a 2-second timeout; a failure or a
117	  timeout is logged and the create still answers 201.
118	- **Rationale**:
119	  - The contract has no job-name constant and BullMQ needs one, so the queue name is reused rather than
120	    inventing a name.
121	  - Exponential backoff with a 1-second base retries after about 1 s and 2 s, so the third attempt ends
122	    about 3 seconds after creation — inside SC-004's 10 seconds.
123	  - BullMQ ignores an `add` whose job id already exists, which is what FR-021 relies on. Completed and
124	    failed jobs are therefore kept (no `removeOnComplete` / `removeOnFail`).
125	  - Without a bound, an `add` against an unreachable Redis can wait longer than the gateway's 5-second
126	    NATS timeout *(verified: `NATS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000`)*, which would turn a stored booking into
127	    a 503. The spec requires 201.
128	- **To verify during implementation**: how `queue.add` behaves with Redis stopped (quickstart scenario
129	  9). The timeout makes the answer correct in either case.
130	- **Alternatives considered**: enqueueing inside the transaction (Redis is not transactional with
131	  Postgres); an outbox table with a relay (recovery is explicitly outside this feature).
132	
133	## R7. Confirmation processing in the worker
134	
135	- **Decision**: A BullMQ processor on `booking-confirmation` delegates to a `ConfirmationService`:
136	  1. Ask the `booking` service for the booking (`booking:findBookingById`). `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` → end
137	     the job normally, without retries. Any other failure is thrown, so BullMQ retries.
138	  2. Booking already `SENT` or `FAILED` → end the job, report nothing.
139	  3. `attempt = job.attemptsMade + 1` *(verified: BullMQ increments `attemptsMade` when an attempt
140	     fails)*.
141	  4. `SimulatedConfirmationSender` decides from the address domain and the attempt number (FR-024).
142	  5. Success → report `SENT` with `attempt`. Failure on the last attempt → report `FAILED` with
143	     `attempt`. Failure with retries left → report `PENDING` with `attempt`, then throw so BullMQ
144	     schedules the retry.
145	- **Rationale**: The job payload is only `{ bookingId }` and the worker has no database, so it must ask
146	  for the address. Deriving the attempt number from the job keeps the worker stateless.
147	- **Alternatives considered**: putting the address in the job payload (the contract fixes the payload);
148	  keeping the attempt count in the worker (lost on restart).
149	
150	## R8. Recording the confirmation outcome idempotently
151	
152	- **Decision**: One conditional statement in the booking repository: update `confirmation_status` and
153	  `confirmation_attempts` where `id` matches, the current status is `PENDING` and the current attempts
154	  are not greater than the reported attempts. The handler then answers the booking as stored, or
155	  `null` when the booking no longer exists.
156	- **Rationale**: A single statement needs no transaction and gives FR-025 directly: a final booking is
157	  never changed, attempts never go down, a repeated report is a no-op, and a report for a deleted
158	  booking changes nothing.
159	- **Why the handler must answer a value**: a Nest request/response handler that returns `undefined`
160	  makes the caller's observable complete without a value *(verified: `client-proxy.js`
161	  `createObserver`)*, which `lastValueFrom` rejects. The same applies to `booking:deleteBooking`, which
162	  answers the deleted `BookingDto`.
163	- **Alternatives considered**: read–check–write in the service (needs a lock to be safe against a
164	  repeated report).
165	
166	## R9. Update rule for the stored pair of times
167	
168	- **Decision**: An update with no fields returns the stored booking unchanged. Otherwise the repository
169	  runs one conditional `UPDATE … RETURNING` that applies the sent fields only when the resulting
170	  `ends_at` is later than the resulting `starts_at`. When no row is returned, the service reads the
171	  booking to choose between 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` and 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`. The table also
172	  carries a `CHECK (ends_at > starts_at)` constraint as a last line of defence.
173	- **Rationale**: Two concurrent updates, each changing one time, cannot together store an invalid pair,
174	  and no transaction is needed.
175	- **Alternatives considered**: read, check in the service, then write (open to that race).
176	
177	## R10. Rejecting `roomId` and `organizerEmail` on update
178	
179	- **Decision**: The `PATCH` body uses a handler-level `ValidationPipe({ transform: true, whitelist:
180	  true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true })`.
181	- **Rationale**: The gateway's global pipe only strips unknown fields *(verified:
182	  `configure-gateway-app.ts`)*, which would answer 200. Changing the global pipe would change
183	  `GET /api/rooms`, whose spec expects unknown query fields to be dropped.
184	- **Assumption**: any unknown field on `PATCH` answers 400, not only those two. On `POST`, unknown
185	  fields are still dropped silently.
186	
187	## R11. Times: parsing, storage and output
188	
189	- **Decision**: Times are stored as `timestamp with time zone` and answered with `toISOString()`. The
190	  `booking` service turns each time into an instant with `new Date(value)`; a value that passes
191	  `IsISO8601({ strict: true })` but does not parse (for example a week date) is answered 400
192	  `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`.
193	- **Assumption**: clients send an offset or `Z` (the web page always does). A date-time without one is
194	  read by JavaScript's rules in the service's time zone; the contract DTO cannot be tightened inside
195	  this feature.
196	
197	## R12. Errors forwarded from the `room` service
198	
199	- **Decision**: The `booking` service's `RoomClient` re-raises an `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`
200	  rejection as an `RpcException`. The type guard `isErrorResponse` moves from
201	  `rpc-exception.filter.ts` into its own exported file in `libs/backend-common` so the booking service
202	  and the worker can reuse it.
203	- **Rationale**: A NATS error reaches the caller as a plain object, and a Nest microservice answers
204	  anything that is not an `RpcException` as a generic internal error; the 404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` would be
205	  lost on its way to the gateway.
206	
207	## R13. Where entities and migrations live
208	
209	- **Decision**: `BookingEntity` and `IdempotencyKeyEntity` go in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/entities`,
210	  with two new migrations next to the existing ones; both are added to `data-source.ts` and exported.
211	- **Rationale**: That is where `RoomEntity` and its migrations are, and `pnpm run migration:run` reads
212	  that data source. Only `libs/contract`, `apps/room` and the `/rooms` page are frozen.
213	- **No foreign key** from `bookings.room_id` to `rooms`: rooms belong to another service and the room
214	  check is made over NATS, as FR-010 requires.
215	
216	## R14. Web page
217	
218	- **Decision**:
219	  - Form state and validation with `react-hook-form`, `yup` and `@hookform/resolvers`; the key from
220	    `uuid` (`v4`). All four are already dependencies.
221	  - `useIdempotencyKey` keeps the key in a ref: created on the first submit, kept when the request
222	    fails without an answer, dropped when the request was answered or any form field changes.
223	  - "Answered" is told apart by type: the existing API client throws `ApiError` only when the API
224	    answered and rethrows the raw error otherwise *(verified: `api-client.ts`)*.
225	  - Start and end use `datetime-local` inputs; values go to the API through `toISOString()` and are
226	    shown with `toLocaleString()`.
227	  - The room filter and the room names come from `listRooms(1, MAX_PAGE_SIZE)`, the existing service
228	    function, unchanged. The table pages at `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`.
229	- **CORS**: the gateway's `enableCors({ origin })` already allows the `Idempotency-Key` request header
230	  and the `PATCH` and `DELETE` methods through the default preflight handling. `Idempotency-Replayed`
231	  is not exposed to browser code; the page does not need it.
232	
233	## Observation outside this feature
234	
235	`apps/room/src/room/room.repository.ts` computes `skip` as `(page - 1) * DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` instead of
236	`(page - 1) * limit`, so `GET /api/rooms?page=2&limit=5` returns rooms 11–12 instead of 6–10. The
237	bookings page only requests page 1, so it is not affected, and the `room` service is frozen for this
238	feature (FR-033). It is recorded here so it can be handled as a separate change.

1	# Data Model: Meeting-Room Bookings
2	
3	**Feature**: `specs/001-room-bookings` | **Date**: 2026-11-10
4	
5	Wire shapes are the classes in `libs/contract` and are not repeated here. This document covers what is
6	stored, the rules on it and the state changes.
7	
8	## Booking — table `bookings`
9	
10	Entity `BookingEntity` in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/entities/booking.entity.ts`. Owned by the
11	`booking` service.
12	
13	| Column | Type | Rules |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| `id` | `uuid` | primary key `PK_bookings_id`, default `gen_random_uuid()` |
16	| `room_id` | `uuid` | not null; no foreign key (see research R13) |
17	| `title` | `character varying(120)` | not null; 1–120 characters |
18	| `organizer_email` | `character varying(320)` | not null |
19	| `starts_at` | `timestamp with time zone` | not null |
20	| `ends_at` | `timestamp with time zone` | not null |
21	| `confirmation_status` | `character varying(10)` | not null, default `PENDING`; `CK_bookings_confirmation_status` limits it to `PENDING`, `SENT`, `FAILED` |
22	| `confirmation_attempts` | `integer` | not null, default 0 |
23	| `created_at` | `timestamp with time zone` | not null, default `now()` |
24	| `updated_at` | `timestamp with time zone` | not null, default `now()`; set on every change to the row |
25	
26	Constraints and indexes:
27	
28	- `CK_bookings_time_range`: `ends_at > starts_at`.
29	- `IDX_bookings_starts_at` on (`starts_at`, `id`) — the unfiltered list.
30	- `IDX_bookings_room_id_starts_at` on (`room_id`, `starts_at`, `id`) — the list filtered by room.
31	
32	Mapping to `BookingDto`: column names become camelCase; the four times are answered with
33	`toISOString()`.
34	
35	### Validation rules
36	
37	| Rule | Enforced by | Answer |
38	|---|---|---|
39	| Field shapes (FR-008) | gateway validation pipe with `CreateBookingDto` / `UpdateBookingDto` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
40	| Unknown field on update | handler-level pipe on `PATCH` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
41	| A time that does not parse to an instant | `booking` service | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
42	| `endsAt` later than `startsAt` on create (FR-009) | `booking` service; `CK_bookings_time_range` behind it | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
43	| Resulting pair valid on update (FR-009) | conditional update in the repository; the service chooses the answer | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
44	| Room exists on create (FR-010) | `booking` service asks `room:findRoomById` | 404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` |
45	| Booking exists on read, update, delete | `booking` service | 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` |
46	
47	### List
48	
49	Ordered by `starts_at` ascending, then `id` ascending so pages are stable. `skip = (page - 1) * limit`,
50	`take = limit`. An optional `roomId` restricts both the rows and the total.
51	
52	### Confirmation state
53	
54	```text
55	                 report SENT (attempts n)
56	   PENDING ───────────────────────────────▶ SENT      (final)
57	     │  ▲
58	     │  └── report PENDING (attempts n)     attempts rises, status stays
59	     │
60	     └──────────────────────────────────▶ FAILED    (final)
61	                 report FAILED (attempts 3)
62	```
63	
64	A report is applied only when the stored status is `PENDING` and the stored attempts are not greater
65	than the reported attempts. Consequences:
66	
67	- `SENT` and `FAILED` never change.
68	- `confirmation_attempts` never goes down.
69	- The same report applied twice leaves the same state.
70	- A report for a booking that no longer exists changes nothing.
71	
72	Updating or deleting a booking does not touch its confirmation state and does not create or cancel a
73	job.
74	
75	## Idempotency record — table `idempotency_keys`
76	
77	Entity `IdempotencyKeyEntity` in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/entities/idempotency-key.entity.ts`.
78	Owned by the `booking` service.
79	
80	| Column | Type | Rules |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| `key` | `uuid` | primary key `PK_idempotency_keys_key`; the `Idempotency-Key` value |
83	| `request_fingerprint` | `character(64)` | not null; sha256 hex of the five create fields in a fixed order |
84	| `response_status` | `smallint` | not null; the stored HTTP status (201) |
85	| `response_body` | `jsonb` | not null; the `BookingDto` answered by the first request |
86	| `created_at` | `timestamp with time zone` | not null, default `now()` |
87	
88	Rules:
89	
90	- A row is written only in the same transaction that inserts the booking, so a row always means a
91	  completed create. There is no status column: "in progress" is the open claim transaction, held as
92	  two transaction-scoped advisory locks (research R3).
93	- No foreign key to `bookings`: the stored answer must survive the booking being updated or deleted
94	  (replay is a snapshot).
95	- Rows are never deleted or expired (FR-019).
96	- Failed validation, an unknown room and an unavailable `room` service store nothing (FR-018).
97	
98	### Claim outcomes
99	
100	The repository's claim returns one outcome; the service maps it to the answer.
101	
102	| Outcome | Condition | Answer |
103	|---|---|---|
104	| `CREATED` | no row for the key; booking and row inserted | 201 with the booking; job enqueued |
105	| `REPLAYED` | row with the same fingerprint | stored status and body, `Idempotency-Replayed: true`; nothing enqueued |
106	| `KEY_REUSED` | row with another fingerprint, or the key is being claimed with another body | 422 `UNPROCESSABLE.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` |
107	| `IN_PROGRESS` | the same key and body are being claimed now | 409 `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` |
108	
109	## Room — table `rooms` (read-only)
110	
111	Existing `RoomEntity`, owned by the `room` service. Not changed. The `booking` service reads a room
112	only through `room:findRoomById`; the web page reads rooms only through `GET /api/rooms`.
113	
114	## Confirmation job — queue `booking-confirmation` (Redis, not Postgres)
115	
116	| Property | Value |
117	|---|---|
118	| Job name | `QueueEnum.BOOKING_CONFIRMATION` (the contract defines no job name) |
119	| Job id | `confirmationJobId(bookingId)` |
120	| Payload | `ConfirmationJobDto` — `{ bookingId }` |
121	| Attempts | `CONFIRMATION_JOB_ATTEMPTS` (3) |
122	| Backoff | exponential, `CONFIRMATION_BACKOFF_MS` (1000 ms) |
123	| Retention | kept after completion or failure, so a second `add` with the same id is ignored |
124	
125	## Confirmation outcome — message, not stored
126	
127	`RecordConfirmationResultDto` — `{ bookingId, status, attempts }`, sent by the worker on
128	`booking:recordConfirmationResult` after every attempt.
129	
130	| Organizer address | Attempt 1 | Attempt 2 | Attempt 3 | Final booking |
131	|---|---|---|---|---|
132	| ends in `@retry.example` | `PENDING`, 1 | `PENDING`, 2 | `SENT`, 3 | `SENT`, 3 |
133	| ends in `@bounce.example` | `PENDING`, 1 | `PENDING`, 2 | `FAILED`, 3 | `FAILED`, 3 |
134	| any other | `SENT`, 1 | — | — | `SENT`, 1 |
135	
136	## Migrations
137	
138	Added in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/database/migrations/` and registered in `index.ts`:
139	
140	- `1731200000002-create-bookings.ts`
141	- `1731200000003-create-idempotency-keys.ts`
142	
143	Both entities are added to `data-source.ts` and exported from `libs/backend-common/src/index.ts`.

1	# Contract: Service Messages and Queue
2	
3	Patterns, queue name and payload classes come from `@roombook/contract`. The contract fixes the request
4	payloads; where it defines no answer class, the answer below reuses an existing contract class.
5	
6	Errors cross NATS as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }` raised through `ExceptionHelper`.
7	
8	## Handled by the `booking` service
9	
10	| Pattern | Request | Answer | Errors |
11	|---|---|---|---|
12	| `booking:createBooking` | `CreateBookingMessageDto` | `CreateBookingResultDto` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`, 404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM`, 409 `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`, 422 `UNPROCESSABLE.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, 503 `UNAVAILABLE.SERVICE` |
13	| `booking:listBookings` | `ListBookingsQueryDto` | `PagedBookingsDto` | — |
14	| `booking:findBookingById` | `BookingIdMessageDto` | `BookingDto` | 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` |
15	| `booking:updateBooking` | `UpdateBookingMessageDto` | `BookingDto` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`, 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` |
16	| `booking:deleteBooking` | `BookingIdMessageDto` | `BookingDto` (the deleted booking) | 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` |
17	| `booking:recordConfirmationResult` | `RecordConfirmationResultDto` | `BookingDto` as stored after the report, or `null` when the booking no longer exists | — |
18	
19	Notes:
20	
21	- `CreateBookingResultDto.replayed` is `true` when the answer came from the stored response; the
22	  `booking` in it is then the stored snapshot, not the current row.
23	- Every handler answers a value. A handler that answered nothing would leave the caller without a
24	  reply (research R8), which is why delete answers the deleted booking and the confirmation report
25	  answers `null` rather than nothing.
26	- `booking:recordConfirmationResult` never raises for a missing or already final booking; it changes
27	  nothing and answers the stored state.
28	- The `booking` service trusts the shape of its payloads: the gateway validates HTTP input, and the
29	  worker builds its report from contract types.
30	
31	## Sent by the `booking` service
32	
33	| Pattern | To | Request | Answer | Used for |
34	|---|---|---|---|---|
35	| `room:findRoomById` | `room` | `RoomIdMessageDto` | `RoomDto` | the room check on create; 404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` and 503 `UNAVAILABLE.SERVICE` are passed on to the caller |
36	
37	## Sent by the `worker` service
38	
39	| Pattern | To | Request | Used for |
40	|---|---|---|---|
41	| `booking:findBookingById` | `booking` | `BookingIdMessageDto` | reading the organizer address and the current confirmation status |
42	| `booking:recordConfirmationResult` | `booking` | `RecordConfirmationResultDto` | reporting the outcome of every attempt |
43	
44	## Queue `booking-confirmation`
45	
46	| | |
47	|---|---|
48	| Producer | `booking` service, once per created booking, after the create transaction commits |
49	| Consumer | `worker` service |
50	| Job name | `QueueEnum.BOOKING_CONFIRMATION` |
51	| Job id | `confirmationJobId(bookingId)` |
52	| Payload | `ConfirmationJobDto` — `{ bookingId }` |
53	| Options | `attempts: CONFIRMATION_JOB_ATTEMPTS`, `backoff: { type: 'exponential', delay: CONFIRMATION_BACKOFF_MS }` |
54	
55	Processing of one attempt (`attempt` = attempts already made + 1):
56	
57	| Situation | Report to `booking` | Job result |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| Booking not found | none | completes; no retry |
60	| Booking already `SENT` or `FAILED` | none | completes |
61	| Sender succeeds | `SENT`, `attempt` | completes |
62	| Sender fails, retries left | `PENDING`, `attempt` | fails; retried after the backoff |
63	| Sender fails on the last attempt | `FAILED`, `attempt` | fails; no retry |
64	| `booking` service does not answer | none | fails; retried if attempts are left |
65	
66	Sender rule (`RETRY_EMAIL_DOMAIN`, `BOUNCE_EMAIL_DOMAIN`): an address ending in `@retry.example`
67	succeeds from attempt 3; ending in `@bounce.example` never succeeds; any other address succeeds on
68	attempt 1. Nothing is sent anywhere.
69	
70	## Health
71	
72	Unchanged: `health:booking`, `health:room` and `health:worker` already exist and are exposed as
73	`GET /api/health/<service>`. This feature adds no deployable service.
